title: Monodromy of a local system on germs over a finite etale neighbourhood
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $\Pi=\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring killed by an integer $n>0$, and let $L$ be an $R_S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] which is a local system in the sense of [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy]: its underlying sheaf of sets is a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of sheaves represented by finite etale $S$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Give $L_{\bar s}$ the monodromy action of that node. Let $u:U\to S$ be a finite etale morphism, let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ satisfy $u\bar x=\bar s$, and let $z\in L(U)$. Regard $\bar x$ as an element of the finite geometric fibre $|U_{\bar s}|$, with its natural $\Pi$-action from the fibre functor [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Writing $\operatorname{germ}_{\bar x}(z)$ for the class of $z$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar x)$ in $L_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], one has
$$g\cdot\operatorname{germ}_{\bar x}(z)=\operatorname{germ}_{g\cdot\bar x}(z)\qquad(g\in\Pi).$$
Neither $R$ nor the stalks of $L$ are required to be finite, and $U$ need not be connected or Galois.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3 and its proof, p. 301 (PDF p. 307): the monodromy action is the extension of the finite-etale fibre functor to ind-objects; its naturality applied to the sheaf map represented by a section on a finite etale neighbourhood.
